items.title: U.S. stock futures slip as chances of rate hike rise after Warsh’s Jackson Hole comments
items.description: U.S. stock-index futures declined on Sunday, as investors ponder the likelihood of a fresh interest-rate hike and look ahead to fresh labor data and tech earnings this week.

items.title: ‘It’s the ultimate regifting’: My mom gave me a house. Should I transfer it back to her to reduce capital gains?
items.description: “The property is very old and requires significant ongoing maintenance.”

items.title: ‘My main goal is to help people’: I’m single, 74, with $10 million burning a hole in my pocket. What should I do?
items.description: “I also own my home and an SUV outright, with no outstanding debt.”

items.title: ‘I feel shoehorned’: My father funded my $800,000 Roth IRA. Does that give him the right to say how I invest it?
items.description: “His argument is essentially that, since my parents provided the money for the Roth, they have a say in how I invest it.”

items.title: My mother, 91, has dementia. Every bank says I need her signature to unlock her $100,000 stock certificate. What can I do?
items.description: “These shares are the only assets in her estate without designated beneficiaries.”

items.title: My contractor handed my $42,000 pool upgrade to a subcontractor I had already rejected. What can I do?
items.description: “I specifically rejected Contractor A because of his reputation.”

items.title: Does a 2% beneficiary inherit 100% if the 98% beneficiary dies in a car accident? Asking for a friend.
items.description: “I’m curious what would happen if the account owner were to die suddenly at the same time as the 98% beneficiary.”

items.title: Am I too old for Roth conversions? I’m 84 and my wife is 77. We have $8 million saved.
items.description: “We are reluctant to pay a financial adviser 2% of assets — roughly $160,000 per year.”

items.title: These charts show how leverage-happy investors are transforming the stock market
items.description: A rush of retail investors and quant funds has caused a shift toward more borrowed money and more short-term trading.

items.title: Party balloons could become a ‘luxury’ as the Iran war spurs a helium shortage
items.description: Dollar Tree says a helium squeeze has hit sales of balloons and party supplies. Researchers note this could foreshadow higher costs for other industries that depend on the gas.
